name: Vadim Novinsky
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Vadim Novinsky owns Ukraine's Smart Holding Group, which has a 24% stake in Rinat Akhmetov's iron ore producer Metinvest.
Novinsky started working in Ukraine in the mid 1990s with Russian oil producer Lukoil, then began buying Ukrainian metallurgy companies.
The Russian native got his Ukrainian citizenship in 2012; he has been a member of parliament since 2013.
Long seen as one of Ukraine's most Putin-friendly billionaires, he tried to jump-start negotiations with Russia before the invasion.
He visited Mariupol with Akhmetov in February 2022 and briefly returned to Kyiv but apparently took off hours before the invasion; he is now suspected to be in Estonia.
forbes_facts: His wife and four children are all Russian citizens and live in St. Petersburg, Russia.

name: Christina Ong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2017-2018); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Husband and wife Ong Beng Seng and Christina Ong are one of Singapore's most influential couples.
Ong is managing director of Singapore-listed Hotel Properties, which owns the Four Seasons and Hilton hotels in Singapore, among much else.
Christina runs Como Hotels & Resorts, retail empire Club 21 and London-listed handbag maker Mulberry.
forbes_facts: The Ongs were embroiled in a family dispute with Christina's siblings, Peter Fu Chong Cheng and Juanita Fu but settled out of court.
Their daughter, Melissa, is a director at Mojo Partners, their family office fund.

name: Wang Mingwang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Mingwang is the co-founder of China electronics maker Sunwoda, a supplier of lithium-ion battery modules.
Wang Wei, his brother and co-founder, chairs the Shenzhen-headquartered company.
Sunwoda's customers include Apple and Huawei.

name: Tan Yu Yeh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Tan Yu Yeh gets his wealth from his stake in Mr. D.I.Y, a home improvement retail chain, which he founded in 2005.
The company was listed on the Malaysian stock exchange in 2020 making him and his brother, Tan Yu Wei, both billionaires.
Mr. D.I.Y. has more than 4,000 stores across Asia and Europe.
D.I.Y stores are typically 10,000 square feet and carry products across ten categories including electrical items, stationery and toys.
Tan worked as an engineer and then as a remisier before setting up his home improvement venture.
forbes_facts: He listed the Indonesian subsidiary, Daya Intiguna Yasa, in December 2024 on the Indonesian stock exchange

name: Joachim Ante
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2022); Hurun Global U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Joachim "Joe" Ante is cofounder and chief technology officer of online and mobile game engine company Unity Software.
He owns about 6% of the company,  which listed on the New York Stock Exchange in September 2020.
Ante cofounded Unity in 2004 with two others in Copenhagen; the company has since moved its headquarters to San Francisco.
Some of the world's most popular games were built using Unity's engine, including Pokemon Go, Among Us and Overcooked.
Ante and his cofounders started off creating a game that failed, but realized that their game engine had value for others.
forbes_facts: Ante initially began writing the core of the Unity platform as a teenager.
More than half of the top 1,000 mobile, PC and console games in 2019 were created using Unity's software, according to the company.

name: John Whittaker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2005-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: John Whittaker runs The Peel Group, a large British conglomerate that holds stakes in property, media and infrastructure businesses.
Known as a visionary with a penchant for regeneration projects, Whittaker got his start in the 1970s acquiring cotton mills for their land.
His group has developed several well-known buildings, including Manchester's MediaCityUK and Trafford Centre mall.
The Lancashire-native now lives on the Isle of Man, an island of the North-West coast of the UK.
forbes_facts: A devout catholic, Whittaker reportedly once considered joining the priesthood.

name: Gary Lauder
forbes_bio: Gary Lauder's fortune stems from Est?e Lauder, the cosmetics giant founded by his grandmother.
His father Leonard ran the family's publicly traded company for more than three decades and stepped down as CEO in 1999.
Lauder, who is not involved with the family company, is managing director of Lauder Partners LLC, a Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm.
A venture capitalist since 1985, he has invested in over 60 private companies.
He is the largest investor in Shotspotter, a publicly-traded company whose technology detects and locates gunshots for immediate response.
Lauder is co-inventor of 16 patents, such as text message authentication for social media platforms, a cable TV system, and a heliostat.

name: Jiang Jinhua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2024); Hurun Self-Made Women (2021-2023)
forbes_bio: Jiang Jinhua is vice chair of Flat Glass Group, a Chinese glass manufacturer.
Her husband and Flat Glass Group Chairman Ruan Hongliang is also a billionaire.
The company went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2015.
Jiang holds a MBA from Arizona State University.
